findings.reason: naming the store path to be reused or repaired (and adding it to the write paths) is what tells the worker whether per-entry refusal and per-entry project are a change to the existing writer or a fresh one; without it the node decides this itself and can land a batch that aborts on one refusal, contradicting its own stated behaviour.
findings.text: §28's mechanism says "validates and routes every entry as a single dispatch would, and stores each one on its own. A refused entry does not stop the rest", but the only batch store path that exists, `queue_requests` (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:287, wrapped at reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:2175), takes one `project`/`repo_root` for the whole batch and raises `CrewError` on the first node whose admission findings contain a refusal (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:318-323), aborting the batch; `reckon/crew/dispatch.py` and `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py` are not in §28's declared write paths, so a worker must either edit an ungranted file or reimplement the writer inside the new `dispatch_batch.py`, and the plan says neither
